Below is a step‑by‑step guide to create an **eBay Promoted Listing** (P‑listing) for your tee shop with a **2.5 % bid** (this is the “Promoted listing fee on the final price” you set in your initial bid, not a percentage of your selling price).  

> *Tip:* eBay calculates the final P‑listing fee as **2.5 % of the final sale price**.  
> For example, if a tee sells for £12.00, the fee you pay for the P‑listing is **£0.30** (if you use the default 2.5 %).  
> If you want to guarantee the fee is *exactly* £0.30 no matter the sale price, you’d set a **custom fee** instead—see the “Custom fee” section below.  

---

## 1. Log in & Go to the “Sell” Dashboard

1. Open the eBay app (or desktop site) and sign in.  
2. Tap **Sell** (or click **Sell > List an item**).  
3. If your tee is already listed, open that listing; otherwise create a new one.

---

## 2. Choose “Promoted Listing” in the Pricing Section

While you’re filling out the listing details:  

| Mobile app (latest iOS/Android) | Desktop |
|------------------------------|---------|
| 1️⃣ “Pricing” section – tap **Add a promoted listing**. | 1️⃣ In the **Price** box, tap the three dots (…) → **Add promoted listing**. |

You’ll be taken to the **Promoted listing settings** screen.

---

## 3. Set Your Base (Non‑promoted) Price

Enter the price you’d normally list the tee for (e.g., **£12.00**).  
This is the amount that will appear to shoppers *if* the P‑listing does not win the bid.

---

## 4. Choose the *Promoted Listing* Fee Structure

**A. Standard (2.5 % of final price)**  
- Select **“Promoted Listing”**.  
- eBay will automatically set the fee to **2.5 % of the final sale price** (no manual input).  
- This is the simplest option and the most common for sellers who don’t need a fixed fee.

**B. Custom fee (fixed amount)**  
If you prefer to pay a fixed amount (e.g., £0.30 or £0.50) irrespective of the sale price:  

1. Tap **“Change fee”** → **“Fixed fee”**.  
2. Enter the amount you want (e.g., **$0.30**).  
3. eBay will use that amount as the fee, regardless of the final sale price.

> *Why this matters:*  
> • **Higher final prices** → higher %‑fee but same fixed fee.  
> • **Lower final prices** → lower %‑fee but you pay the same fixed fee.

---

## 5. Launch the Promoted Listing

- Review the preview: you’ll see the *base price* and the fee that will be deducted when the item sells.  
- Tap **“Save & continue”** (mobile) or **“Submit”** (desktop).  

The listing goes live immediately.

---

## 6. Monitor & Optimize

Use the **Promoted Listings Manager** (under **My eBay > Sold items & feedback > Promoted listings**) to:

- See how many impressions, clicks, and conversions the listing has.  
- Adjust your **bid** if you want a higher probability of winning the placement. (Higher bids don’t change the 2.5 % fee, but increase your chance of the promoted spot.)  
- Exclude or add categories, or pause the listing when you’re not actively selling.  

**Tip:** If you notice your P‑listing gets many impressions but few clicks, try lowering the base price slightly or improving the title/description/SEO.

---

## 7. Troubleshooting Common Issues

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|----------|--------------|-----|
| “Promoted listing fee too high” | eBay is calculating 2.5 % of a very high final price. | Either lower the final price or choose a *fixed fee* option. |
| Listing won’t go live | “Promoted listing” option not available in this category or location. | Verify the category supports P‑listing; some categories have restrictions or you may need to move the item. |
| No impressions after 24 h | Listing may not be optimized for the “Promoted” section yet. | Add relevant keywords, use a high‑quality photo, and consider raising your bid slightly. |
| You’re being charged a fee higher than 2.5 % | You may have selected a *Category* or *Platform* that overrides the default fee. | Go to **Project Settings** → **Promoted listings** and check the fee schedule. |

---

## 8. Quick FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I use a 2% fee instead of 2.5%?** | No – eBay’s default for new sellers is 2.5%. You can only go **higher** (e.g., 3%) if you want to bump up placement odds. |
| **Will paying the 2.5 % fee reduce my profit?** | Yes, but it also boosts visibility. For tees that sell quickly (e.g., over £20) the fee is modest (£0.50). |
| **Do I need to set a daily budget?** | No. eBay charges you the fee only on **sold** items, not for exposure. |

---

### Bottom Line

- **Step 1:** Create the listing.  
- **Step 2:** Enable “Promoted Listing.”  
- **Step 3:** Let eBay auto‑apply 2.5 % (or set a fixed fee).  
- **Step 4:** Submit, monitor, and adjust bids as needed.

Happy selling! 🚀 If you have any follow‑up questions—about optimizing titles, choosing categories, or anything else—just let me know.
